subject.title: acp: assistant text corrupted when Gateway revises in-progress output (non-append revision mis-sliced)

question: How should the ACP bridge represent Gateway `replace=true` revisions when standard ACP message and thought chunks cannot retract already-emitted text?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the externally consumed ACP contract makes the repair shape a product/protocol choice rather than a safe mechanical slice replacement.

options.title: Choose conservative ACP buffering
options.body: Delay or buffer provisional ACP text when Gateway replacement semantics are possible so clients end the turn with the authoritative final text without relying on a non-standard retract operation.

options.title: Use a documented extension
options.body: Emit replacement metadata or a client-specific capability only if maintainers are willing to document fallback behavior for clients that ignore it.

options.title: Accept new-message fallback
options.body: Emit replacement snapshots under a new `messageId`, accepting that some clients may show both stale and corrected text instead of one corrected answer.

recommendation.title: Choose conservative ACP buffering
recommendation.body: Delay or buffer provisional ACP text when Gateway replacement semantics are possible so clients end the turn with the authoritative final text without relying on a non-standard retract operation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the ACP bridge and are the strongest history signal for choosing cross-protocol ACP behavior.
